battle.name: 第一次馬達加斯加戰爭
battle.theater: 東岸土阿馬西那與貝齊米塔特拉河
battle.brief: 一八八三年五月，法國以梅里納王國驅逐南部法商為由，封鎖東岸港口土阿馬西那，奪取對岸諾西法利島；海軍陸戰隊與外國軍團沿貝齊米塔特拉河深入，在安基菲中伏，兩艘砲艇全滅。遠洋鐵甲艦泊在深水外海無從插手，內陸全靠小艇與步兵；一八八五年比西縱隊直逼首都，十二月以條約收場。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 木殼外面包了鐵。裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。

countries: 交戰的一方是法國第三共和國。總理朱爾·費里自一八八三年執政，海軍部長夏爾·德·弗雷西內以殖民警務名義主導遠征，一八八四年一月起戰爭部長由布唐格接掌，並在海軍與陸軍之間設立專門的遠征指揮部。參戰兵力以海軍陸戰步兵為主，輔以外國軍團、從西非調來的塞內加爾土著射手與殖民地民兵，另有隨軍報務與醫療人員；海軍方面由印度洋分遣隊與遠征艦隊擔任封鎖、登陸、沿岸輸送與艦砲支援，並在土阿馬西那與莫倫達瓦設立領事館，商人公司「馬達加斯加公司」與「馬達加斯加協會」在西南海岸的特許權益成了法方的經濟藉口。另一方是梅里納王國：一八八三年八月前由女王拉納瓦洛納二世統治，她死後由年幼的拉納瓦洛納三世即位，攝政太后拉索赫里納與外交大臣拉伊南德里亞馬潘德里主持國政。王國的武裝以王軍與徵召的民兵為主，砲兵仍用舊式滑膛前裝銅砲，步槍多為各國舊式前裝槍，另有大量標槍；西南部的薩卡拉瓦諸部在梅里納高壓統治下屢有騷動，把王國的兵力牽制在南部。英國與德國在島上各有商業與傳教利益，但沒有出兵干涉；英國的傳教士與德國商人反過來向法方施壓，成為法國加快動手的助力。
countriesEn: One of the parties was the French Third Republic. Jules Ferry was prime minister from 1883, and the Minister of the Navy Charles de Freycinet directed the expedition in the name of the colonial service; in January 1884 the Ministry of War passed to General Boulanger, and a special expedition command was set up between the navy and the army. The troops were mainly marine infantry, supported by the Foreign Legion, Senegalese tirailleurs brought up from West Africa, and colonial militia, with signallers and medical staff attached; at sea the Indian Ocean station and the expedition squadron handled the blockade, the landings, coastal transport and naval gunfire support, and consulates were opened at Toamasina and Morondava, while the concessions held on the southwest coast by the Compagnie de Madagascar and the Société de Madagascar provided the economic pretext for French claims. The other party was the Merina Kingdom: until August 1883 it was ruled by Queen Ranavalona II, and after her death by the child queen Ranavalona III, with the regent Rasoherina and the minister for foreign affairs Rainandriamampandry directing affairs of state. The kingdom's armed force consisted of the royal army and militia levied from the population; its artillery still used old smooth-bore muzzle-loading bronze guns, its rifles were mostly obsolete muzzle-loaders of various foreign types, and it also had a great many spears. The Sakalava peoples of the southwest rose repeatedly under the harsh Merina rule, which tied royal troops down in the south. Britain and Germany each had commercial and missionary interests on the island, but neither intervened militarily; British missionaries and German merchants instead pressed the French to act, and this helped to speed up the decision to go to war.
people: 法國方面，總理朱爾·費里是這場戰爭的政治推手：他不斷批准增兵與遠征，把原本海上的封鎖升格為內陸的遠征，最後卻在一八八五年三月因戰事無功與財政壓力而下台。戰爭部長布唐格把戰爭當成政治資本，散布「馬達加斯加復仇」的口號，法國國內反體制運動因此挾戰事聲勢而壯大。海軍上將阿納托爾·德·比西在最後一役率縱隊深入，於一八八五年逼近首都北面的安達菲亞瓦拉特拉王營，最後代表法方與梅里納方面簽訂條約。馬達加斯加方面，女王拉納瓦洛納二世於一八八三年八月去世，其女拉納瓦洛納三世年幼即位，攝政太后拉索赫里納掌權，外交大臣拉伊南德里亞馬潘德里代表王廷與法方談判，多次拒絕撤走英國傳教士，也拒絕承認法國在南部的權益。十九世紀初奠定中央集權與閉關鎖國國策的安德里亞納普瓦伊納梅里納與拉納瓦洛納一世，其陰影仍籠罩著一八八○年代的王廷。早年的先驅如留尼汪商人拉扎爾·帕斯卡爾，曾於一八六○年代上溯高原，勸說王廷開放口岸，是法國殖民政略最早的推手之一。
peopleEn: On the French side, the prime minister Jules Ferry was the political driving force: he kept authorising reinforcements and expeditions, raised a blockade into a campaign inland, and in the end fell from office in March 1885 because the war had achieved little and the financial strain was mounting. The war minister Boulanger turned the campaign into political capital and popularised the slogan of revenge in Madagascar, and the anti-government movement in France grew louder on the strength of the war. The admiral Anatole de Bussy led the final column inland in the last phase, reached the royal camp of Andafiavaratra north of the capital in 1885, and finally signed the treaty on the French side. On the Malagasy side, Queen Ranavalona II died in August 1883 and her daughter Ranavalona III, still a child, succeeded her; the regent Rasoherina held power, and the minister for foreign affairs Rainandriamampandry conducted the negotiations with the French, repeatedly refusing to withdraw the British missionaries or to concede French rights in the south. Andrianampoinimerina and Ranavalona I, who in the early nineteenth century set the course of centralisation and closure to the outside world, still cast their shadow over the court of the 1880s. Among the earlier pioneers was Lazare Pascal, a merchant from Réunion, who went up to the highlands in the 1860s and argued for opening the ports, and who is counted as one of the first promoters of the French colonial project in Madagascar.
kits: 卡面上的鐵甲艦屬一八六二年前後的歐洲主力艦世代：木質船身外面加裝鐵質裝甲帶，或改用全鐵船身配旋轉砲塔，裝甲第一次比火砲更難對付，砲塔設計從此繞著裝甲轉。到一八八○年代，這一世代的鐵甲艦已明顯過時：英國首艘遠洋鐵甲艦「勇士」號於一八八三年付諸退役，法國的帶甲鐵甲艦多留於本土封存待用，但它們仍是列強在遠東互相威懾的信用。馬達加斯加的實際戰鬥卻用不上它們：東岸沙岸平直、內河淺而湍急，鐵甲艦吃水深、轉向遲鈍，連海灣都難以進出，遠征隊因此依賴吃水淺的砲艇與汽艇、海軍陸戰步兵與外國軍團，以及大量當地腳夫。真正投入的火力是兩艘可沿河行進的砲艇「哈什」與「亞塔干」，它們在貝齊米塔特拉河上游被梅里納部隊擊沉，艇上乘員幾乎全滅，成為法國輿論的導火線；法軍另以舊式木殼巡洋艦與護衛艦執行封鎖、登陸與沿岸砲擊，並以野戰砲與山砲支援縱隊。梅里納方面以滑膛前裝銅砲守備河口與關隘，槍械多為前裝步槍，另有大量標槍；火藥與槍械多靠沿海貿易取得，供應一旦被封鎖即告吃緊。
kitsEn: The ironclad on the card belongs to the generation of European capital ships of about 1862: a wooden hull with an iron belt fitted over it, or an all-iron hull with revolving turrets, so that armour for the first time was harder to defeat than guns, and turret design turned around it from then on. By the 1880s this generation of ironclad was clearly out of date: Britain's first seagoing ironclad, HMS Warrior, was paid off in 1883, while France's belt ironclads mostly lay in reserve in European waters; they remained, however, the credit on which the powers in the Far East still leaned. The actual fighting in Madagascar could not use them. The east coast is flat and sandy, the inland rivers are shallow and fast, and ironclads draw too much water and turn too slowly to enter even the bays, so the expedition depended on shallow-draft gunboats and steamers, on marine infantry and the Foreign Legion, and on a great many local porters. The only heavy firepower committed was in two river-capable gunboats, the Hache and the Yatagan, which were destroyed by Merina troops in the upper Betsimitatatra with almost their whole crews lost, and this became the flashpoint of French public opinion. The French also used old wooden-hulled cruisers and avisos for the blockade, for the landings and for coastal bombardment, and they brought field and mountain guns forward with the columns. On the Merina side the defence of the river mouths and the passes rested on smooth-bore muzzle-loading bronze guns; the small arms were mostly muzzle-loading rifles, with a large number of spears, and both powder and firearms came largely through coastal trade, so that supply tightened at once the coast was blockaded.
tactics: 法軍的打法分兩層：海上以封鎖切斷梅里納的對外貿易，把王國逼到只能靠內陸資源撐下去；陸上則以縱隊沿東岸公路與河谷向內陸推進，海軍陸戰步兵與外國軍團打先鋒，步槍手以小分隊散開搜索，砲艇在河道中殿掩護，後面跟著載有野戰砲、給養與病員的車隊以及數百名腳夫。一八八三年深入貝齊米塔特拉河的縱隊只有數百人，隊形拉得太長，在河道彎曲處遭梅里納兵伏擊而覆滅；此後法軍改為集中兵力、步步為營，推進速度反而更慢，在雨季與叢林裡消耗了大量時間與體力。梅里納軍隊避免與法軍正面決戰，退守堅固的土木砲台與河岸工事，以小股兵不斷襲擾縱隊的側翼與補給，切斷道路，延燒村莊與田禾，使遠征隊因糧秣不足與熱病而減員；國王一系則在最後主動放棄首都外圍，率朝廷退往高原內陸，令法軍只能占領空城與王營。一八八五年最後一次遠征，法軍以大縱隊直趨塔那那利佛，路線、給養與腳夫都預先備妥，梅里納軍卻始終不接戰，戰爭遂以談判收場。
tacticsEn: The French fought on two levels. At sea they blockaded to cut off the Merina's foreign trade and force the kingdom to live on its own interior resources. On land they drove columns inland along the coast road and up the river valleys, with marine infantry and the Foreign Legion leading, riflemen searching in small scattered squads, gunboats covering from the river in the centre of the column, and behind them wagons carrying field guns, supplies and sick, together with several hundred porters. The column that went up the Betsimitatatra in 1883 numbered only a few hundred men and was strung out too far; it was ambushed by the Merina in a bend of the river and destroyed. After that the French concentrated their force and advanced by bounds, and the pace became slower still, so that months were lost in the rains and in the forest. The Merina avoided meeting the French in open battle: they fell back on earthwork batteries and riverbank fortifications, harried the flanks and the supply line with small bodies of men, cut the roads, and burned the villages and the standing crops, so that the expedition suffered from want of food and from fever. The royal side at the end deliberately gave up the approaches to the capital and withdrew the court into the interior, leaving the French to occupy an empty city and the royal camp. In the last expedition of 1885 the French marched a great column straight for Tananarive, with the route, the supplies and the porters all prepared in advance, and the Merina never once accepted battle, so that the war ended in negotiation.
data: 時間自一八八三年五月法國宣布封鎖、奪取土阿馬西那外海的諾西法利島起，至一八八五年十二月十二日在土阿馬西那簽訂條約止，前後約兩年半，其中真正交火集中在兩年之內。距離方面，土阿馬西那至首都塔那那利佛的道路長約三百公里，貝齊米塔特拉河全長數百公里，縱隊在這樣的路程上要靠腳夫輸送十數天。兵力上，一八八三年首次登陸的遠征隊為數千人規模，其中海軍陸戰步兵佔多數；一八八五年最後一次深入內陸的縱隊在法方記載中為數千人，比首戰更大，仍以海軍步兵與外國軍團為骨幹。梅里納能召集的兵力在法方估計中從一萬到數萬不等，但分散在廣闊的內陸與南部。砲兵方面，法軍出動的是野戰砲與山砲，數目為數十門；梅里納的滑膛銅砲射程短、對遠射無效，只能守近海與關隘。戰爭對法國財政的負擔以特別撥款計算，金額達數千萬法郎，成為一八八五年內閣倒台的直接理由之一。法軍的減員以熱病與腸病為主，各次遠征的病亡數目在法方報告中沒有完整統計，戰陣上的傷亡反居其次。
dataEn: The war ran from May 1883, when France announced the blockade and seized the island of Nosy Faly off Toamasina, to the treaty signed at Toamasina on 12 December 1885, about two and a half years in all, with the actual fighting concentrated inside two of them. As for distance, the road from Toamasina to the capital Tananarive is about three hundred kilometres, and the Betsimitatatra is several hundred kilometres long; a column moving over that road needed ten-odd days for its transport to be carried by porters. On numbers of men, the expedition that first landed in 1883 was of the order of several thousand, marine infantry forming the majority; the column that went deepest inland in 1885 is recorded on the French side as several thousand strong, larger than the first, still built on marine infantry and the Foreign Legion. The forces the Merina could raise are estimated by the French anywhere from ten thousand to several tens of thousands, but they were spread over a wide interior and the south. In artillery the French brought up field and mountain guns to the number of several dozen; the Merina's smooth-bore bronze pieces had short range and were useless at long distance, and could only hold the near coast and the passes. The financial burden on France was carried as special credits running into tens of millions of francs, and this was one of the direct reasons the government fell in 1885. French losses came above all from fever and dysentery; no complete record of sickness deaths survives in the French reports, and battle casualties came second.
cause: 起因是多層的。最遠的一層是一八三○年代以來梅里納王國的閉關政策：安德里亞納普瓦伊納梅里納與拉納瓦洛納一世把外來商人、教士與傳教士擋在內陸之外，只在東岸的土阿馬西那與南部海岸留下幾個貿易點，歐洲商船只能買賣鯨油與奴隸，得不到礦產與土地。這一政策在法國殖民政略興起後便難以維持：一八六○年代法國公司取得西南海岸的開礦與貿易權，一八七○年代梅里納王國向薩卡拉瓦地區用兵，把南方的補給線與傳教站收進王國版圖，等於直接動了法國商人的地盤。引爆點是一八八三年初梅里納當局驅逐南部的法國商人、封閉其商行、拒絕賠償被扣的產業與財產，法國領事館屢次交涉無效。一八八三年三月法國內閣更替，新政府把此事列為必須解決的殖民問題。同時女王在八月去世，留下年幼的繼承人與攝政太后，法國判斷王廷內部正弱，是施壓的最好時機。最後一層是戰略的：馬達加斯加扼守印度洋東緣，控制它便能威脅莫三比克海峽與紅海航路，也能把英國通印度的航線往前推一步；德國商人在南部購地設站，法方文件記作某位 Baron 的購地，更讓法國擔心南方要衝會先被別人拿走。
causeEn: The origins had several layers. The oldest is the closure policy of the Merina Kingdom since the 1830s: Andrianampoinimerina and Ranavalona I kept foreign merchants, priests and missionaries out of the interior and left only a few trading points on the east coast at Toamasina and in the south, so that European shipping could buy whale oil and slaves but could obtain neither minerals nor land. That policy became untenable once the French colonial project got under way: in the 1860s French companies obtained mining and trading rights on the southwest coast, and in the 1870s the Merina kingdom campaigned against the Sakalava regions and folded the southern supply lines and mission stations into the kingdom, which struck straight at the ground the French merchants held. The spark was the expulsion of the French merchants from the south in early 1883, the closure of their trading houses and the refusal to compensate for property seized; the French consulate pressed the matter repeatedly and in vain. The cabinet changed in March 1883, and the new government listed the affair among the colonial questions that had to be settled. The queen died in August, leaving a child heir and a regency, and France judged that the court was divided and weak, the best moment to apply pressure. The last layer was strategic: Madagascar commands the eastern edge of the Indian Ocean, and holding it would threaten the Mozambique Channel and the Red Sea route and would push forward by one step the British line to India; German merchants buying land and setting up stations in the south, one of them a baron whose purchase the French documents record, made the French afraid that the southern approaches would be taken by someone else first.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果並未讓法國得到馬達加斯加，卻改變了兩個政權的行為方式，也改變了十九世紀末歐洲殖民政略的節奏。對法國而言，遠征得不償失：花掉數千萬法郎，換來的只是一份承認法國在東岸若干據點與商權的條約。國內由此產生對殖民地冒險的懷疑，費里內閣在一八八五年三月垮台，反體制的布唐格運動挾馬達加斯加的戰事聲勢而壯大；法國此後數年在殖民地採取更慢、更小規模的推進，直到一八九四年因一系列摩擦再起戰端，最終以一八九六年的正式兼併收場。對梅里納王國而言，封鎖與內陸遠征暴露了王國的脆弱：從此朝廷不再相信海洋與外來援助，國防重心全數移向高原，軍隊在西方教練之下重建，砲兵與後勤逐漸改進；王廷在喪失沿海門戶後更向內陸收縮，外國傳教與貿易仍被嚴格限制。一八九○年代英國傳教士被逐事件正是這一防禦邏輯的延續，也是第二次法馬戰爭的直接導火線。海上軍備方面，一八八○年代中葉已是後膛速射砲與新式裝甲巡洋艦的時代，鐵甲艦退居海防與本土封存，說明以首都為核心、靠海軍封鎖施壓的殖民主義已到盡頭。
impactEn: The war gave France neither Madagascar nor a decisive settlement, but it changed the behaviour of both states and the tempo of European colonial policy at the end of the nineteenth century. For France the expedition was a bad bargain: tens of millions of francs were spent to obtain a treaty that merely acknowledged French positions and commercial rights on the east coast. The result was a suspicion of colonial adventures at home; Ferry's cabinet fell in March 1885, and the anti-government Boulangist movement, riding the noise of the Madagascar war, grew stronger. France then pursued a slower and smaller colonial advance for several years, until a series of frictions brought the war back in 1894 and ended in the formal annexation of 1896. For the Merina kingdom, the blockade and the inland expedition exposed how fragile the kingdom was: from then on the court no longer trusted the sea or foreign help, the whole weight of defence shifted to the highlands, the army was rebuilt under Western instructors, and artillery and logistics improved by degrees. Cut off from the coast, the court contracted further inland, and foreign missions and trade remained strictly restricted. The expulsion of the British missionaries in the 1890s was a direct continuation of this defensive logic and the immediate spark of the second Franco-Hova war. On naval matters, the middle of the 1880s was already the age of breech-loading quick-firing guns and of new armoured cruisers, and the ironclad had fallen back to coastal defence and to reserve in home waters, which shows that a colonial policy built on blockade and on limited inland expeditions had reached its end.
result: 一八八五年十二月十二日於土阿馬西那簽訂的條約是這場戰爭的終點：法國取得諾西法利島與東岸若干據點，獲得自由通商與在王都派駐領事的權利，並取得一筆賠款；梅里納王國則維持對內陸的完全主權，拒絕接受任何形式的法國保護，也拒絕答應驅逐英國傳教士或德國商人。雙方都沒有達到自己的全部目標：法軍始終未能攻入塔那那利佛，也沒有推翻王廷；梅里納雖保住了國土，卻把沿海的地盤與對外貿易的節點讓了出去。此後法軍陸續撤出部分據點，只留下外交與通商的存在；而王廷在一八九○年代面對傳教衝突時，衝突最後仍引來一八九四至一八九五年第二次馬達加斯加戰爭，一八九六年法國兼併全島，君主制隨之瓦解。因此，一八八三至一八八五年的戰爭不是法國成功的征服，而是使梅里納王國在形式上獨立、實質上被壓進內陸的一場失敗；這一結果本身也說明，當時的殖民政略仍舊靠海軍封鎖與有限遠征解決爭端，很快這種辦法就不夠用了。
resultEn: The treaty signed at Toamasina on 12 December 1885 was the end of the war. France obtained the island of Nosy Faly and several positions on the east coast, the right to trade freely and to station consuls at the royal capital, and an indemnity; the Merina kingdom kept full sovereignty over the interior, refused any form of French protection, and refused to expel the British missionaries or the German merchants. Neither side reached all its aims: the French army never entered Tananarivo and never overturned the court, while the Merina saved their country but gave up the coastal territories and the nodes of their foreign trade. The French afterwards withdrew from some of the positions and kept nothing but a diplomatic and commercial presence; and when the court faced the missionary conflicts of the 1890s, those conflicts in the end brought about the second Franco-Hova war of 1894 and 1895, and the formal annexation of the whole island in 1896, after which the monarchy fell apart. The war of 1883 to 1885 was therefore not a successful French conquest but a defeat that left the Merina kingdom independent in form and pressed in substance into the interior, and the outcome itself shows that the colonial policy of the time still settled disputes with naval blockade and limited expeditions, and that this method would soon not be enough.
